item.text:
## 2B.1 Research Note: Lula, Brazil, 2024

**Bottom line:** The 2024 record is strongly pro-diplomacy. Lula repeatedly chose negotiation, ceasefire language, and multilateral de-escalation where peaceful alternatives clearly existed. I found limited counterevidence in the form of sharp rhetoric and one peace initiative later criticized as exclusionary, but not a pattern of force-first behavior.

### Accepted claims

- **Claim:** Lula treated peace talks on Ukraine and Gaza as the default response in a high-level U.S. meeting.
  - **Title:** [Lula said he discussed peace in Ukraine and Gaza with Antony Blinken](https://noticias.uol.com.br/ultimas-noticias/reuters/2024/02/21/lula-diz-que-discutiu-conflitos-em-gaza-e-na-ucrania-em-encontro-com-blinken.htm)
  - **Publisher:** Reuters via UOL
  - **Date:** February 21, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://noticias.uol.com.br/ultimas-noticias/reuters/2024/02/21/lula-diz-que-discutiu-conflitos-em-gaza-e-na-ucrania-em-encontro-com-blinken.htm
  - **Claim-level summary:** Lula said he discussed peace in Ukraine and Gaza with Antony Blinken, and Planalto separately reiterated his desire for peace and an end to the conflicts. This is direct evidence that he preferred diplomacy when peaceful channels were available.
  - **Question IDs:** `2B.1`; also `1B.1`, `1B.8`

- **Claim:** Brazil and China’s Ukraine initiative explicitly framed diplomacy and a ceasefire as the path forward.
  - **Title:** [Brazil and China sign joint proposal for peace negotiation in the Russia-Ukraine war](https://noticias.uol.com.br/ultimas-noticias/reuters/2024/05/23/brasil-e-china-assinam-proposta-conjunta-de-negociacao-de-paz-para-guerra-da-ucrania-e-russia.htm)
  - **Publisher:** Reuters via UOL
  - **Date:** May 23, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://noticias.uol.com.br/ultimas-noticias/reuters/2024/05/23/brasil-e-china-assinam-proposta-conjunta-de-negociacao-de-paz-para-guerra-da-ucrania-e-russia.htm
  - **Claim-level summary:** The joint statement said dialogue and negotiation were the only viable solution and called for conditions to resume direct talks and move toward a comprehensive ceasefire. That is strong evidence against force-first instincts.
  - **Question IDs:** `2B.1`; also `1B.1`, `1B.4`, `1B.8`

- **Claim:** Lula used the UN General Assembly to argue for direct dialogue and against militarized escalation.
  - **Title:** [Speech by President Lula at the opening of the 79th UN General Assembly in New York](https://www.gov.br/g20/en/documents/speeches/speech-by-president-lula-at-the-opening-of-the-79th-un-general-assembly-in-new-york)
  - **Publisher:** Brazil G20 / Ministry of Foreign Affairs
  - **Date:** September 24, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://www.gov.br/g20/en/documents/speeches/speech-by-president-lula-at-the-opening-of-the-79th-un-general-assembly-in-new-york
  - **Claim-level summary:** Lula warned that nuclear arsenals and destructive weapons were pushing the world toward confrontation and said direct dialogue was crucial. In crisis terms, that is a clear preference for de-escalation over force.
  - **Question IDs:** `2B.1`; also `1B.1`, `1B.2`, `1B.8`

- **Claim:** Lula repeatedly framed the Gaza and Ukraine crises as problems for negotiation, not military solution.
  - **Title:** [President Lula's speech at the Summit of the Future opening in New York](https://www.gov.br/g20/en/documents/speeches/president-lulas-speech-at-the-summit-of-the-future-opening-in-new-york)
  - **Publisher:** Brazil G20 / Ministry of Foreign Affairs
  - **Date:** September 22, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://www.gov.br/g20/en/documents/speeches/president-lulas-speech-at-the-summit-of-the-future-opening-in-new-york
  - **Claim-level summary:** Lula said the world could not go back to living with nuclear threats and tied his warning to arms-race criticism and multilateral reform. This reinforces a pattern of preferring diplomatic off-ramps.
  - **Question IDs:** `2B.1`; also `1B.1`, `1B.2`, `1B.8`

### Counterevidence / caveats

- **Claim:** Lula’s Gaza rhetoric was highly confrontational and worsened diplomatic relations with Israel.
  - **Title:** [Lula repeats that the Israeli government commits genocide in Gaza and defends the creation of a Palestinian state](https://noticias.uol.com.br/ultimas-noticias/reuters/2024/02/23/lula-repete-que-governo-israelense-comete-genocidio-em-gaza-e-defende-criacao-de-estado-palestino.htm)
  - **Publisher:** Reuters via UOL
  - **Date:** February 23, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://noticias.uol.com.br/ultimas-noticias/reuters/2024/02/23/lula-repete-que-governo-israelense-comete-genocidio-em-gaza-e-defende-criacao-de-estado-palestino.htm
  - **Claim-level summary:** Lula repeated the genocide accusation and defended Palestinian statehood, triggering a major diplomatic rupture. This is the main cautionary item, but it is still rhetoric and diplomacy-breaking, not evidence that he preferred force over peaceful alternatives.
  - **Question IDs:** `2B.1`; also `1B.2`, `1B.8`

- **Claim:** The Brazil-China Ukraine initiative was criticized by Kyiv as exclusionary and “destructive.”
  - **Title:** [Ukraine's Zelenskiy dismisses 'destructive' China-Brazil peace initiative](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/ukraines-zelenskiy-dismisses-destructive-chinabrazil-peace-initiative-3612966)
  - **Publisher:** Reuters via Investing.com
  - **Date:** September 12, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/ukraines-zelenskiy-dismisses-destructive-chinabrazil-peace-initiative-3612966
  - **Claim-level summary:** Zelenskiy said Kyiv was not included and that the proposal lacked respect for Ukraine’s territorial integrity. This weakens the good-faith quality of the initiative, though it still points to de-escalation rather than force-first behavior.
  - **Question IDs:** `2B.1`; also `1B.4`, `1B.8`

### Search gap

I did **not** find reliable 2024 evidence that Lula treated force as the preferred first option in any major crisis I searched. The 2024 record I found is dominated by:
- dialogue,
- ceasefire proposals,
- multilateral mediation,
- and explicit anti-escalation language.

So the evidence base supports a **clear yes** on 2B.1, with the main caveat being that some of Lula’s rhetoric was confrontational and one peace initiative drew serious criticism from Ukraine.
